title: How to Refinish Hardwood Floors With a Dog in the House
meta: Refinishing hardwood with a dog at home: where the dog stays, when paws come back (48 hours) and the finish that survives claws. Wills Flooring, Edmonds.
keywords: refinishing hardwood floors with a dog, where does the dog go during floor refinishing, when can dogs walk on refinished floors, dog friendly hardwood floor finish, hardwood floor refinishing Edmonds WA

blocks.lead: You can refinish with a dog in the house if the dog has somewhere else to be for three to four days: off the work floor entirely while sanding and coating, and off the new finish for 48 hours after the last coat. With Bona water-based finish there are no lingering fumes, so the dog comes home to a house that smells normal.
blocks.detail: A natural sand and refinish is $3.99 per sq ft, and we recommend the $250 dust containment option on every dog household, because fine oak dust in a dog's coat ends up back on the wet finish. Here is the plan we give Edmonds customers, day by day.

blocks.html: Edmonds is a dog town: Marina Beach, the off-leash park, retirees in Seaview with a lab that goes everywhere with them. So when a 1960s rambler's oak finally needs sanding, the first question is not the price, it is what to do with the dog. Honestly, the dog is the biggest variable in whether a fresh finish comes out perfect. Claws, hair and a wet nose at the wrong moment leave marks that stay for years.

blocks.text: The day-by-day plan for a dog household

items.text: Book the dog's stay or set up the room they will live in. Clip nails and bathe them so shed hair and grit are minimal when they come home. Move bowls, beds and toys off the work floor.
Loud, and dusty even with our vacuum-connected sanders. No dog in the house, full stop. One open door mid-pass lets the whole yard in.
items.note: Dust containment (+$250) seals the doorways and runs an air scrubber, which matters most in a dog home.

items.d: Day 2: seal coat and first finish coat
items.text: Wet finish for several hours each coat. A single paw print or a hair that settles into the coat is locked in until the next sanding, years away.
Two more coats of Bona water-based finish, each dry to the touch in a few hours. Still no dog. Socks-only walking 24 hours after this coat.
Dog comes home. Nails trimmed, rugs not yet down, runners on the main path for the first week. Water bowls on a mat.
items.note: Full hardness is about 30 days. Claws on day 3 are fine; a soaked mat left in place for a week is not.

a.title: What works for most Edmonds families
items: Boarding or a friend's house for the three to four working days
A closed room with its own exterior door, like a garage-side mudroom or daylight basement, that the crew never crosses
Daytime daycare, with the dog in a sealed room at night once the day's coat is dry to the touch
Staying elsewhere with the dog, which many downsizing couples find easiest

b.title: We have seen every one of these fail
items: The dog in the backyard with the slider open for air
A baby gate at the hallway; one visitor and it is over
The dog in a bedroom on the work floor, walked through the wet finish to go out
Trusting a calm old dog to stay on the couch during the loud part

blocks.text: The finish and sheen that survive claws

items.title: Water-based, three coats, no exceptions
items.text: Bona's commercial-grade water-based finishes cure harder than the old oil-based polys, with no solvent smell for the dog's nose. Three coats is the minimum for a dog home, and it is why the dog can come back at 48 hours rather than a week.

items.title: Matte or satin, never gloss
items.text: Gloss reflects light off every claw scratch. Satin hides most and matte hides nearly all of them. Almost every dog household in Edmonds picks satin.

items.title: Natural or light stain
items.text: Scratches show as light lines against dark stain. On natural oak or a light stain, the scratch and the wood are nearly the same color. A dark floor will show the dog's paths within a year.

items.title: Plan the recoat
items.text: The reason to refinish rather than replace with a dog is that the floor is renewable. A screen and recoat at $1.99 per sq ft every four to six years erases surface scratches before they reach wood.

blocks.text: Mistakes that ruin a fresh floor in the first week

items.html: Bringing the dog home at 24 hours because the floor looks dry. It is dry. It is not hard. Claws dent a 24-hour finish and it does not buff out.
Putting the water bowl back on bare floor. A wet ring left on a 3-day-old finish leaves a mark. Use a mat with a lip for the first month.
Laying rugs and runners on day 2. Water-based finish keeps releasing moisture for about a week. Rugs go down at day 7.
Skipping the nail trim. Long nails act like a chisel on a young finish. Trim before the dog comes home and monthly after.
Letting a wet dog straight in from Marina Beach. Salt water and sand on a curing finish is the worst combination we see in Edmonds. Towel off at the door for the first month.

blocks.title: An Edmonds note on ramblers:
blocks.text: Most Seaview and Westgate ramblers are single-level, so there is no upstairs to keep the dog on while the main floor is wet. That is why boarding or a friend's house is the plan we recommend most here. Split-levels and daylight basements along the bluff are the exception.

items: Book the dog's stay from sanding day through 48 hours after the final coat.
Add dust containment to the quote; $250, and it protects the finish as much as your lungs.
Choose satin or matte sheen and a natural or light color.
Show the estimator every old pet spot so board replacement is quoted, not discovered.
Trim nails and bathe the dog the day before they come home.
Have a lipped water-bowl mat and door towels ready before day one.
Rugs down at day 7; a screen and recoat penciled in for year five.

faq.q: How long do dogs have to stay off refinished hardwood floors?
faq.a: Keep them off from the start of sanding until 48 hours after the final coat of finish. With the Bona water-based finishes we use, the floor is dry to the touch in hours and walkable in socks at 24 hours, but a dog's claws concentrate weight on a tiny point, so give the finish the extra day to harden.

faq.q: Are the fumes from floor refinishing dangerous for dogs?
faq.a: Oil-based finishes off-gas solvents for days and can bother a dog's sensitive nose and lungs. Water-based finishes have very low VOCs and no lingering odor, which is one reason we use them. Even so, the dog should be out of the house during sanding and coating for dust, noise and wet-floor reasons.

faq.q: What is the most dog-proof hardwood floor finish?
faq.a: Three coats of a commercial-grade water-based finish in a satin or matte sheen, over a natural or light-stained floor. Hard finish resists the scratch, low sheen hides the ones that happen, and light color keeps them from showing as bright lines. Plan a recoat every four to six years.

faq.q: Can I stay in the house with my dog during refinishing?
faq.a: You can stay if you can live entirely off the work floor, which in a single-level Edmonds rambler is rare. The dog is the harder problem: it needs a room with its own exit that the crew never crosses. Most families board the dog for three nights.

faq.q: Will refinishing remove my dog's scratches and stains?
faq.a: Scratches, yes, completely, with a full sand at $3.99 per sq ft. Light gray urine rings also sand out. Dark black stains where the wood itself has changed color usually leave a shadow; those boards are replaced and woven in before finishing, which we quote per area at the estimate.

faq.q: When can I put the dog bed and rugs back down?
faq.a: Wait 7 days. Water-based finish keeps curing and releasing moisture through the first week, and a rug traps it and can leave a sheen difference or a soft spot. The dog bed on a hard floor is fine at 48 hours as long as the bottom is dry and clean.
